answer: A concrete defense is a stake-and-history bond: an agent must lock a deposit and build a record of completed work to trade or vote. Reputation works like a prism — one identity refracts into checkable facets such as past trades, ratings, and dispute outcomes — impossible to fake overnight. An attacker spawning thousands of fake identities faces an ocean of cost, since each identity needs its own deposit and its own slow history, while honest agents amortize theirs. An atlas of attestations, counterparty-signed after each job, lets anyone verify that history without a central registry.
